name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Plasma Cutter PC-X1 'Dragon's Breath'
description: An experimental weapon that fires a bolt of superheated plasma contained within a magnetic bottle that maintains cohesion for approximately 40 meters before dissipating. The PC-X1 generates plasma by ionizing a hydrogen gas cartridge with an intense electrical arc, then magnetically accelerating the plasma bolt through a shaped barrel. On impact, the magnetic containment fails and the plasma expands explosively, producing a burst of thermal energy sufficient to melt through composite armor and ignite anything flammable within a 1-meter radius. The weapon is loud, visually spectacular, and tactically impractical at anything beyond close-medium range — but within that envelope, nothing survives a direct hit.
specifications:
plasma temperature: approximately 15,000°C at generation
effective range: 5-40 meters before containment dissipation
power source: Hydrogen gas cartridge + electrical arc generator
shots per cartridge: 4
recharge between shots: 8 seconds
weight: 7.5 kg
thermal bloom on impact: 1-meter radius
acoustic signature: 165 dB at muzzle — extremely loud
prototypes: 6 units in field testing
story_hooks: An armored convoy was destroyed by what witnesses describe as a bolt of fire that melted through the lead vehicle — the plasma impact signature on the wreckage is unmistakable.
One of the six PC-X1 prototypes has gone missing from Zheng-Dao's weapons lab and the security footage for that night has been erased — someone inside the company walked it out.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist energy weapon with an aggressively angular profile. The PC-X1 resembles a hybrid between a military plasma rifle and industrial cutting torch — all sharp lines, protruding cooling fins, and a barrel assembly that dominates the gun's proportions. Visually top-heavy despite balanced weight distribution.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 78 cm | Width: 18 cm (at widest cooling fin) | Height: 12 cm | Barrel length: 32 cm with magnetic shroud
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and substantial — 7.5 kg feels like holding a chunk of industrial equipment. Balanced toward the barrel, requiring two-handed grip for sustained aiming, but not unwieldy once shouldered.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-aluminum alloy frame with embedded magnetic acceleration coils. Cooling fins cast from reinforced steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with heat-stressed discoloration streaking along the barrel shroud. Magnetic coil access panels show satin chrome underneath worn protective coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body with burnt-orange heat weathering around the barrel assembly. Accent lines of exposed copper coiling visible through access slots.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with shallow spiral grooves for sweat management. Wrapped with frayed copper wire at wrist anchor — functional heat dissipation aid rather than design choice.
distinctive_features: Magnetic containment barrel shroud with prominent cooling fins angled backward
Exposed copper electrical conduits running along the left side of frame
Hydrogen cartridge slot on right side with pressure-gauge window (glowing blue when charged)
Arc ignition chamber visible through titanium inspection plate — faint crackling visible during standby
Three stacked heat-sink vanes along top rail, discolored orange-brown from thermal cycling
Safety interlock lever beneath trigger guard with worn warning symbols
Capacitor bank bulge under the stock — pulsing faintly with stored electrical charge
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO HEAVY INDUSTRIES stamped into left side of frame in serif block letters. Serial number (PC-X1-███) etched in reverse below manufacturer stamp. Experimental designation 'β-6' handwritten in gold paint on stock.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Light impact scarring on barrel shroud, thermal stress discoloration heavy but not pitted. Electrical components show signs of recent recalibration — fresh capacitor fluid residue near coil access panel. Cartridge slot shows repeated use wear.
